text:
sam_acme: Hi team — started getting a bunch of 429s around 09:12 UTC. Our app uses a single API key but runs behind a proxy/NAT. Total traffic from the key is ~20 req/min, so not sure why we're hitting limits.

alex_support: Thanks — can you paste the exact 429 response headers (Retry-After, x-*limit headers) and an example request? Are you sending the key in Authorization header or query param?

sam_acme: Posting example: curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk.acme.123\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat\" -d '{\"input\":\"ping\"}'

---
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
x-rate-limit-scope: ip
x-rate-limit-ip: 203.0.113.45
x-rate-limit-key: 600/min
x-rate-limit-org: 10000/min
Content-Type: application/json

{\"error\":\"rate_limited\",\"message\":\"ip exceeded burst quota\"}

sam_acme: We see x-rate-limit-key shows high allowance, but x-rate-limit-ip shows IP-burst exhausted. Our egress NAT IP is shared. Is that expected?

alex_support: That fits with current heuristic — we compute quotas by evaluating multiple scopes (api_key, project, org, ip) and apply the first failing scope by precedence. However, the precedence can vary depending on how the request is authenticated and whether we see a forwarded client IP.

maria_sre: Quick clarifying Qs: 1) Is your proxy setting X-Forwarded-For or are requests NATed (single IP) without header? 2) Are you mixing keys across projects under the same org? 3) Any recent config changes on the proxy?

sam_acme: 1) NATed; proxy does not set X-Forwarded-For. 2) Single key across service. 3) No changes.

alex_support: Ok. If X-Forwarded-For isn't present, our edge attributes the request to the egress IP. If that IP is shared across many teams, you can hit the IP bucket even if the key quota is fine. This is expected behavior, but we should make sure the response clearly indicates which scope blocked you. Looks like the body says \"ip exceeded burst quota\" so it's the IP scope.

sam_acme: That makes sense — the surprising part is we used to see key-scoped throttles for this workload, not IP. Did something change in precedence?

alex_support: Not intentionally. There was a heuristics tweak last month to prefer key/project scoping when an Application header is present, but fall back to IP when we detect NAT with missing forwarded headers. Could be a regression.

maria_sre: Can you reproduce locally with a curl loop from a machine that shares the same NAT? To debug, run: 
for i in $(seq 1 40); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code} %{url_effective}\\n\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk.acme.123\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings; done

and check which iterations 429 starts on. Also capture response headers with -D - .

sam_acme: Will try and share results in ~15m.

[~12m later]

sam_acme: Repro done. 429 starts at iteration 18 consistently. Headers: Retry-After 20, x-rate-limit-scope: ip, x-rate-limit-ip: burst=20/60s, x-rate-limit-key: 600/min. Sending directly from a machine with unique IP does not 429.

alex_support: Good repro — this confirms IP-burst. Two paths forward: 1) If you can set X-Forwarded-For on the proxy with the original client IP, we can optionally prefer forwarded client IP for scoping (but that has security considerations), or 2) request a quota bump / dedicated IP pool for your org (we can route you to Dedicated or reserved egress).

sam_acme: We cannot set X-Forwarded-For in our managed proxy. Is there an interim server-side option we can request to prefer key-scoping for your org while we fix infra?

jordan_platform: Tagging platform eng — @maria_sre is this something we can do as an account-level override? We have a precedent for a temporary override that biases scoping to key/project where org asserts a stable key-per-service.

maria_sre: We can do a scoped override, yes, but need to validate no-one else on the same NAT will be impacted. I'll need the org ID + an example NAT IP range to lock to. Also flagging potential billing implications: if we ignore IP scoping you might exceed org units unexpectedly.

sam_acme: Org ID: org_98765. NAT IP range: 203.0.113.40/29. Happy to accept billing caveat.

alex_support: I'll open an internal ticket for an override and escalate if we spot precedence regression. Adding logs to ticket: request IDs, sample headers. @jordan_platform please review override risk.

jordan_platform: Saw the ticket. Quick note: we had a change in the routing code that re-ordered scope evaluation to check ip before key in some fast-paths when the request lacked forwarded headers — that explains the behavioral flip. I'm going to PR a small fix to respect API key precedence when a valid key is present.

rate-limiter-bot: new incident created: INC-2028 - ip-vs-key-scoping-regression. Assigned to platform/team-rate-limit.

alex_support: For immediate unblock I've requested a temporary org-level override mapped to your NAT block. Should be in place within 30–45m. I'll update here when active.

[~40m later]

alex_support: Override applied. Can you run your repro and confirm 429s stop?

sam_acme: Re-tested — no 429s for 500 requests, looks good. Thanks! :tada:

maria_sre: Leaving follow-up: we will roll the precedence fix to stable in the next patch and close INC-2028 when validated in staging. Also documenting: prefer key/project > org > ip by default unless explicit config says otherwise.

sam_acme: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please let me know if you need any more logs.

alex_support: Closing loop here but keeping ticket open until the code fix lands. If you see any billing anomalies after override, ping us immediately.

jordan_platform: PR opened -> https://git.internal/redwood/platform/merge_requests/451. Marking for cherry-pick to stable.

sam_acme: :thumbsup:
